'''Hideo Aoki''' is a Japanese [[theoretical physicist]].  He is an [[emeritus professor]] at the [[University of Tokyo]], Japan, and works in the field of [[condensed-matter physics]] and cold-atom physics.

==Biography==
Hideo Aoki studied theoretical condensed-matter physics, and received his [[PhD]] in physics from the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1978, where his doctoral research was on the [[quantum Hall effect]].  He was a visiting scholar at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], [[University of Cambridge]], UK in 1980-1982.  He then built up his group in 1986 at the department of physics, [[University of Tokyo]] in theoretical condensed-matter physics, as a full professor from 1998.<ref name="CP">{{Cite journal |last=Aoki |first=Hideo |date=2025-10-02 |title=Flat bands in condensed-matter systems – perspective for magnetism and superconductivity |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00107514.2025.2550105 |journal=Contemporary Physics |volume=66 |issue=1-4 |pages=1–38 |doi=10.1080/00107514.2025.2550105 |issn=0010-7514|url-access=subscription |arxiv=2510.13098 }}</ref>

In 2016 he retired from the [[University of Tokyo]] and became an emeritus professor, and subsequently took up a research position at [[National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology]] (AIST), Tsukuba, Japan until 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aoki Group {{!}} The University of Tokyo |url=http://cms.phys.s.u-tokyo.ac.jp/index_eng.html |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=cms.phys.s.u-tokyo.ac.jp}}</ref> In 2017 he was a guest professor at [[ETH Zurich]], Switzerland, and also a guest scientist at the Max-Planck-Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter, Hamburg in Germany in 2018.<ref name="CP" />

==Research==
The theoretical works of Hideo Aoki and his group<ref>{{Cite web |title=Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Hideo+Aoki%22 |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> are focussed on many-body and topological effects in electron systems, namely, [[superconductivity]], [[magnetism]], and topological systems (including [[graphene]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Optical quantum Hall effect in graphene |url=https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/focus/en/articles/a_00158.html |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=The University of Tokyo |language=en}}</ref>).  For these system he explored materials designed for correlated electron systems, and in particular non-equilibrium phenomena in recent years. He has authored or co-authored over 300 articles<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cms.phys.s.u-tokyo.ac.jp/dissertation_en.html|accessdate=2020-09-02|title=Hideo Aoki Publications}}</ref> ranging across condensed-matter physics. He has also authored or co-edited six books:<ref>H. Kamimura and H. Aoki: Physics of Interacting Electrons in Disordered Systems (International Series of Monographs on Physics 76), Oxford University Press, Oxford, 1989). https://global.oup.com/academic/product/physics-of-interacting-electrons-in-disordered-systems-9780198520238</ref><ref>H. Aoki, M. Tsukada, M. Schluter and F. Levy (editors): New Horizons in Low-Dimensional Electron Systems (in the series Physics and Chemistry of Materials with Low-Dimensional Structures), Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht, 1992).</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics Meets Mineralogy |url=https://www.cambridge.org/universitypress/subjects/earth-and-environmental-science/mineralogy-petrology-and-volcanology/physics-meets-mineralogy-condensed-matter-physics-geosciences |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=Cambridge University Press & Assessment |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2014 |editor-last=Aoki |editor-first=Hideo |editor2-last=S. Dresselhaus |editor2-first=Mildred |title=Physics of Graphene |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-02633-6 |journal=NanoScience and Technology |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-02633-6 |issn=1434-4904|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>Hideo Aoki: Integer quantum Hall effect in R. Fornari (Ed.): Comprehensive Semiconductor Science and Technology, 2nd Edition, Vol. 1, pp. 134-189 (Elsevier, 2025).</ref><ref>T. Chakraborty, Ana M. Sanchez, Hideo Aoki, Robert H.
